executiveSummary: The reporting period features multiple high-urgency, operational incidents that expand both the scale and sophistication of synthetic-media-enabled crime and influence. Microsoft disrupted the EvilTokens AI-powered phishing service after confirmed compromise of over 12,000 accounts across more than 10,000 organizations, underscoring the growing role of AI in account takeover operations View Article . Separately, an autonomous multi-agent campaign reportedly targeted hundreds of online retailers, compromising at least 27 companies and stealing over 600,000 payment cards from two victims View Article . Public-safety and election-security risks are also acute. Manhattan prosecutors seized 12 domains in a takedown of commercialized deepfake pornography that victimized more than 1,200 people View Article , and AP reporting highlights active use of AI-generated political ads in the U.S. 2026 midterms amid inconsistent disclosure rules View Article . Additional reporting signals government-focused voice-impersonation risks to senior U.S. officials Source , and state-aligned influence efforts in Angola View Article . On the defensive and regulatory fronts, content provenance and detection capabilities continued to improve with OpenAI and Microsoft API-level verification features and Adobe workflow support for C2PA metadata View Article Vendor Advisory Supporting Report . In Europe, new guidance and a Code of Practice detail machine-readable marks and implementation measures for labeling and detecting AI-generated content View Article View Article . Overall, the threat environment appears to be worsening given the number of high-impact incidents, cross-sector victimization, and continued adoption of AI agents for fraud and influence operations, despite parallel progress in provenance and regulatory controls.
